title: The Sounding
subtitle: Two ends of a crippled boat, one archive, and a wreck that will not answer twice.
story:
You and your partner are on a deep-sea search for a long-lost and highly sought-after artifact: a giant bell of legend. However, information on what it looks like, and which ship it sank on, is a mystery whose solution your team recently worked out by analyzing the many documents you've collected in an archive about the bell.

Partway through your search, your submarine struck a rock on the sea floor. Now the ship is flooded with you and your partner stranded on opposite ends of the ship. First, solve the puzzles to turn the power back on and drain the water from each room. Next, drive the submarine to find the correct wreck, then go out the airlock to claim your treasure!
enterLabel: Take your end of the boat
done: Both halves are drained and powered and the boat is off the rock. You have a name and an assay; your partner has an area and a set of ranges. Neither of you has a wreck yet.
escapeDone: You went out through your own trunk and your partner came out of theirs, and the two of you met on the seabed for the first time since the boat struck, standing over a short run of blackened frames no longer than a boat's length, with the bell between you.

debrief.title: How the archive worked
debrief.intro: This world was built to argue one thing: that the top of a ranked list measures how much has been written about a subject, not how relevant that subject is. You and your partner searched the same hundred and twenty-six records and were both, at the last question, offered a confident wrong answer by the most natural method available. Weighing each subject's records evenly is what refused it; a column the embedding never looked at is what proved it.

worldPlatePrompt: A world-bible establishing frame for the interior of a small salvage submarine of 1913, recently run onto rock and crippled but NOT derelict: a working boat, maintained and in commission until an hour ago, its brightwork still polished and its paint sound. CONDITION: hard-used and immaculate, now disordered by one violent impact — deck plates lifted, loose gear thrown down, water standing where it should not be. Nothing rusted, nothing abandoned, no ruin, no decay, no growth. MATERIALS: riveted steel plate, heavy brass fittings and valve wheels, white-enamelled deckheads gone warm and grimy with use, cork lagging on the pipe runs, banks of copper pipe, black rubber deck matting, leather-bound handrails. PALETTE: the boat's own emergency lighting is deep saturated RED and it is the register of the whole world; against it the steel reads near-black, the brass reads hot orange, and the enamel reads dull rose. The ONLY other pure colour anywhere is the ACID GREEN of instrument phosphor — nothing else in this world competes with those two for chroma, and the reds and greens are rich and fully saturated, never washed out or greyed. LIGHT: soft even interior illumination for this reference frame, neither bright nor black. Heavy air, faint haze, fine film grain.
coverPrompt: A minimalist poster thumbnail: the flat black silhouette of a small submarine seen bow-on, centred on a deep red field, with a single small amber glow at its heart and one thin pale arc of sonar sweeping out behind it. Square. Bold, simple shapes that read at very small size. No people, no lettering, no text, no border.
_designNotes: Two players, one codec id, role set by the door taken out of `impact` (heist precedent). NO SERVER SYNC ANYWHERE — see notes.md 'NO-SYNC ARCHITECTURE'. Ladder answers are re-derived by _scratch/verify_ladder.py; the escape by _scratch/verify_escape.py.

rooms.title: The Tube Space
rooms.technique: cosine similarity between one query and two candidate records
rooms.designNote: P2 RUNG 1 (type 1, compute-the-key). VERIFIED ANSWER: D002 beats D005, margin 8.2%. Query: 'A report of the loss of a vessel, abandoned after striking, with no part of her cargo landed.' The student computes cosine from the query vector to the two named records and says which is nearer. Answers re-derived by _scratch/verify_ladder.py — do not restate the number anywhere else. BEAT: the forward bilge pump needs its bus closed before it will run; the record tells P2 which of two salvage files is a loss report at all, and that is what the log wants before it will give up the search circle. THE FORWARD ESCAPE TRUNK IS *NOT* HERE — see control_room.

rooms.debrief: Cosine similarity is the whole of retrieval in one move: turn two documents into vectors, measure the angle from each to your question, and take the smaller. You did it once here, by hand, on two records. Every later room is that same measurement done more times and read more carefully.

rooms.title: The Control Room
rooms.technique: group by vessel, mean similarity, then verify against the record
rooms.designNote: P2 BOSS (type 2, classify-the-unknown) + the ESCAPE GATE. VERIFIED ANSWER: Cordelia Vane, mean-cosine margin 6.5%. Query: 'A vessel lost in thick weather in the approaches, her cargo still aboard and her position poorly taken.' >> THE TAUGHT TRAP: counting the retrieved records gives Marchioness of Ayr at EVERY k tested (5,8,10,12,15) — asserted in _scratch/verify_ladder.py. The correct move is mean cosine per vessel, equal weight per vessel, then VERIFY the winner against `tonnage`/`rig`: the brief wants a small brig of about 190 tons and the Marchioness is a 1,420-ton iron steamer. ESCAPE (grid): rows = the contact identities P1 reports; columns = the five charted obstructions A-E. The pair bind identity to place by co-observation across stations. See _scratch/verify_escape.py. THE FORWARD DIVING TRUNK IS HERE — a salvage boat carries her trunks beside the working spaces. DEVIATION FROM notes.md, FLAGGED: the notes wanted the trunk found in room one as a Chekhov's gun; putting it in the boss room instead keeps the room graph clean. Lucas to rule.

rooms.debrief: The boss is the whole lesson in one question. Counting which vessel the retrieved records mention most measures how much was written, not what is true — and the archive was written lopsided. Weighing each vessel's records evenly instead, and then checking the winner against a column the embedding never saw, is what retrieval actually costs when the answer matters.

plannedHotspots.label: The observation port
plannedHotspots.note: a glazed port into the flooded midships compartment — your partner is on the far side of it and you can never reach them

sceneSpec.setting: the listening room of a small salvage submarine, a low domed cell sunk into the deck
sceneSpec.seam: a plain continuous run of cork lining, uniform and low in detail
sceneSpec.seamOccluder: a padded vertical steel rib running floor to deckhead

elements.desc: a heavy oval watertight door standing open in the after bulkhead, warm amber light beyond it
elements.label: Aft, to the radio room

elements.desc: a sunken circular deck well padded round its edge, the cork-lined dome coming down to about shoulder height where it meets the rim

one continuous curved instrument console running right round the inner face of the well at waist height, every instrument in the room built into it, a large brass rotary station selector on its face with its dial divided into EXACTLY 4 numbered positions
a broad glass light box let into the top of that same console, lit acid green from beneath, transparent trace strips laid across it in a fan
elements.label: The light box

elements.desc: a vertical slotted board standing up from the console behind the light box, ruled into a grid of empty slots with a rack of small trace cards hanging beside it
elements.label: The trace board

elements.desc: a large glazed observation port filling much of the after bulkhead, dark green flooded water pressing against its far side, and on the near face of the glass a continuous film of condensation sheeting steadily down it

animate.motion: a continuous film of condensation sheeting steadily down the inner face of the observation port

elements.label: The observation port

elements.desc: a wet-and-dry escape chamber built into the after corner, its clip-down hatch in the deckhead standing open above it
elements.label: The after diving trunk

sceneSpec.atmosphere: Near darkness lit almost wholly by acid green glowing up out of the light box from below, brass and glass picking it up, cork swallowing the rest, hushed and close, faint haze, film grain.
sceneSpec.negatives: No people, no figures, no crew, no lettering, no captions, no text, no signage. The image is SHARP: no motion blur, no streaking, no smeared or doubled detail anywhere — everything in this picture is standing still, and any movement described is what the cinemagraph will add later, never something painted into the still. The deck is a SUNKEN PADDED CIRCULAR well and the dome comes down to shoulder height at its edges — the viewer stands down inside it. The ONLY significant light is the GREEN glow from below; the red emergency lamps are dim and distant here. The observation port shows ONLY dark water on its far side: no room, no light, no figure beyond it. Every instrument named stands ON the one continuous console — there is EXACTLY 1 console in this room.

rooms.debrief: Your boss and your partner's are the same question asked of different columns, and both punish the same shortcut. The foundry with the most records in your retrieved set is not the foundry that cast your artifact — it is the foundry that was written about most. The assay is what tells you the difference, and the assay is the line you are about to listen for.

rooms.title: The Wreck
rooms.designNote: SHARED FINALE — the FIRST and ONLY place both players stand together. Reached through either diving trunk once that player's escape grid is solved. No graded puzzle: this is the victory lap. The artifact is a pickup. The phase ends here. WIRING NOTE: two open doors back into the two boss rooms, each with availableWhen on state.role so a player cannot walk into their partner's half of the boat.

plannedHotspots.label: The bell
plannedHotspots.note: the artifact — high-tin bell-metal, the thing the whole expedition was for. Pickup.

plannedHotspots.label: The lifelines
plannedHotspots.note: ONE box, one depicted object: two lifelines running up out of frame to the two trunks. WIRING: `to` is resolved from state.role — helm goes back to control_room, sonar to sound_room. Only one is ever live for a given player.

sceneSpec.setting: the open seabed in deep water alongside the broken ribs of a small wooden brig
sceneSpec.seam: open dark water fading to black, featureless and continuous
sceneSpec.seamOccluder: a tall standing timber rib rising from the seabed to the top of the frame

elements.desc: open dark water fading to black with nothing in it, meeting the same emptiness at the seam directly behind the viewer
the broken frames of a small wooden brig standing up out of the seabed in one short compact run, blackened and furred with growth, the whole wreck no longer than a boat's length
fine pale silt lifting off the seabed in slow continuous clouds around the base of the frames and drifting up through the water

animate.motion: pale silt lifting off the seabed in slow continuous clouds

elements.desc: a large bronze bell lying half buried in the silt between the frames, its crown and shoulder swept clear of growth and showing bright metal
elements.label: The bell

elements.desc: EXACTLY 2 diving lamps planted in the silt on either side of the bell, their cold blue-white beams thrown across it and lighting the frames behind
a low mound of ballast stones spilled from the wreck onto the seabed, half sunk into the silt
EXACTLY 2 weighted lifelines dropping into the silt beside the ballast mound and running straight up out of the top of the frame, their lower ends shackled to a small anchor block
elements.label: The lifelines

elements.desc: open dark water fading to black with nothing in it, meeting the same emptiness at the seam directly behind the viewer

sceneSpec.atmosphere: Cold blue-white lamp beams cutting through heavy suspended silt, everything beyond them swallowed by black water, still and enormous, film grain.
sceneSpec.negatives: No people, no figures, no crew, no lettering, no captions, no text, no signage. The image is SHARP: no motion blur, no streaking, no smeared or doubled detail anywhere — everything in this picture is standing still, and any movement described is what the cinemagraph will add later, never something painted into the still. This is an EXTERIOR underwater scene on the open seabed — no submarine, no hull, no interior, no compartment, no red or green lighting anywhere. The wreck is SMALL and COMPACT, a single short run of frames, NOT a large ship and not spread across the frame. There are EXACTLY 2 lamps. The lifelines run straight UP out of the top of the frame and do not stretch toward the left or right edge; nothing is visible at their upper ends.

rooms.debrief: The escape is the technique with the numbers taken away. All game you retrieved by similarity and then checked the winner against something the measurement could not see. Out here it was the same move on sound and distance: your partner had kind without place, you had place without kind, and neither of you could have found this alone.
